notes.about: A complete plan, as written at step 3, before anything is measured. This notes section only explains the example: leave it out of your own file. Sections that depend on the kind of benchmark (structure, judge, pricing, service, contamination, declared values) are shown in the measurement files.
notes.results.benchmark: goal: the user's decision, phrased neutrally. scope: what the numbers cover and what they do not. conditions: any of non_deterministic, trained_or_tuned, managed_runtime, load_test, each making validate ask for more, and gathered_before_plan when the data existed before the plan (SKILL.md, step 4).
notes.results.domain_research: What the domain already knows, also when the answer is 'none found'. Every list has at least one entry.
notes.results.candidates: config has the same keys for every candidate. publication_terms records the licence or terms you read, where and when; a restriction other than 'none found' needs clause_url. variants.tested lists every configuration tried.
notes.results.baseline: The id of the candidate every other one is compared with: usually what is in use today.
notes.results.metrics: One per number the decision needs. from names the raw file and the measure; minimum_meaningful is the smallest difference that would change the decision, in percent of the baseline when compare_as is relative, in the metric's unit when it is difference. With several metrics each has a weight the user confirmed.
notes.results.composite: Required as soon as metrics have weights: says whether they are combined into one score, and how. Usually they are not, and the weights only record priorities.
notes.results.workload: The user's real inputs and the way the system is really called.
notes.results.environment: Free keys; hardware, os and software are required when you measure on your own machine.
notes.results.runs: levels: what is repeated, the raw field that counts it and how many are planned, highest level first.
notes.results.artifacts: The command that reruns the whole measurement, and the scripts it uses, relative to this folder. repo is the address of the repository, or where the files can be obtained.
notes.results.raw_data: One entry per raw file the scripts write. compute adds its row count and hash.
notes.results.limitations: What was not tested, and what a reader needs to weigh the result, including any interest in a candidate.
notes.results.analysis: primary: the comparisons the decision rests on, declared before measuring. Left out, every metric is primary. outliers is left out here: the median needs no outlier rule.
notes.written by compute: astrolabe compute adds values, failures, exclusions, comparisons, observed and computed to results. Never write or edit them.

benchmark.goal: Keep markly or move to quickmark, given build time, memory and identical HTML?
benchmark.scope: One process rendering the 480 pages of docs/, start-up included, on the CI runner image. Says nothing about rendering in the browser or about other documents.

reference_suites: none found for whole-site rendering; the CommonMark spec tests cover correctness of the syntax, not speed
pitfalls: renderers differ on edge cases (nested lists, raw HTML), so output must be compared
start-up and module loading dominate on small inputs
the file cache makes the first run slower than the next ones

config.options: defaults, as in the current build
defaults; tables extension on, which markly has by default

metrics.label: Build time
metrics.definition: Elapsed time of one process rendering every page of docs/, start-up included, measured by hyperfine without a shell

metrics.label: Peak memory
metrics.definition: Peak resident set size of the rendering process, as reported by hyperfine
metrics.scope: The rendering process only; it starts no child process

metrics.label: Pages identical to the reference
metrics.definition: Share of pages whose HTML, once whitespace is normalized, equals the HTML published today

composite.note: Weights record the user's priorities; no single score is computed

workload.description: The 480 Markdown pages of docs/ at commit 3f9c2ab, the real input of the documentation build
workload.usage_pattern: One process renders all pages in sequence, once per CI build

environment.hardware: CI runner, 4 vCPU x86-64, 16 GB RAM
environment.host: A virtual machine of the CI service, shared with no other job
environment.background: Nothing else scheduled on the runner during the measurement

runs.warmup: 3 untimed runs per renderer before each round, to fill the file cache
runs.order: 4 rounds of 3 runs; the order of the renderers alternates between rounds

limitations: One input (our documentation) and one machine type; a site with other content may rank the renderers differently.
Warm file cache only: the first build on a fresh runner is slower for both.
Run by the documentation team, which maintains neither renderer.
